algorithm.title: Low Back Pain: Diagnosis and Management.

cell.label: Acute low back pain. Signs of cauda equina (saddle anesthesia, bowel or bladder dysfunction)?
Major cancer risk factors (new onset pain with history of cancer, multiple cancer risk factors, or strong clinical suspicion)?
Radiographs, sed rate initially, followed by MRI if indicated.
Other red flags (severe or persistent pain, significant neurologic deficit, significant trauma)?
Conservative therapy. Persistent radiculopathy in surgical or epidural injection candidate, or worsening symptoms or red flags at any time?
Continue conservative therapy. Consider physical therapy, massage, treatment for chronic back pain (see chapter).
